method: Primary source comparison; existing IDs retained; source PDFs and fixed dialogue scripts unchanged. No native TTS or release certification.

segments.base: こちらこそどうぞよろしく

added_form.kana_reading: こちらこそどうぞよろしく

changes.before: Group I changes the final i-row sound before masu to the e-row plus masu; Group II adds raremasu to the stem. Shimasu becomes dekimasu and kimasu becomes koraremasu.
changes.after: Group I changes the final い-row sound before ます to the え-row plus ます; Group II adds られます to the stem. します becomes できます and 来ます becomes 来られます.

changes.before: Potential verbs then conjugate as Group II. Wakarimasu already means understand; do not form wakaremasu.
changes.after: Potential verbs then conjugate as Group II. わかります already means understand; do not form わかれます.

changes.before: The potential expresses ability or an opportunity allowed by circumstances. Object wo usually becomes ga; other particles remain.
changes.after: The potential expresses ability or an opportunity allowed by circumstances. Object を usually becomes が; other particles remain.

changes.before: Keep ni in tomodachi ni aemasu.
changes.after: Keep に in 友達に会えます.

changes.before: Miemasu and kikoemasu describe something naturally entering sight or hearing; mark it with ga.
changes.after: 見えます and 聞こえます describe something naturally entering sight or hearing; mark it with が.

changes.before: Miraremasu and kikemasu describe the ability or opportunity to watch or listen intentionally.
changes.after: 見られます and 聞けます describe the ability or opportunity to watch or listen intentionally.

changes.before: Dekimasu can also mean that a building, object or product is completed or comes into existence.
changes.after: できます can also mean that a building, object or product is completed or comes into existence.

changes.before: This differs from ability; a location commonly takes ni.
changes.after: This differs from ability; a location commonly takes に.

changes.before: Only with shika
changes.after: Only with しか

changes.before: Place shika after the limited element and use a negative predicate. Dake with an affirmative need not imply insufficiency.
changes.after: Place しか after the limited element and use a negative predicate. だけ with an affirmative need not imply insufficiency.

changes.before: Shika replaces ga or wo but follows particles such as ni.
changes.after: しか replaces が or を but follows particles such as に.

changes.before: Contrast with wa
changes.after: Contrast with は

changes.before: Wa can contrast two topics, often with ga linking the clauses.
changes.after: は can contrast two topics, often with が linking the clauses.

changes.before: Wa after another particle
changes.after: は after another particle

changes.before: Wa commonly replaces ga and wo; it may follow ni, de or kara to topicalize or contrast a circumstance.
changes.after: は commonly replaces が and を; it may follow に, で or から to topicalize or contrast a circumstance.

changes.before: Retain a necessary relation such as kara in koko kara wa.
changes.after: Retain a necessary relation such as から in ここからは.

changes.before: Miemasu or kikoemasu
changes.after: 見えます or 聞こえます

changes.before: Masu stem plus nagara joins simultaneous actions by the same person. The second is the main activity.
changes.after: ます stem plus ながら joins simultaneous actions by the same person. The second is the main activity.

changes.before: Habits with te imasu
changes.after: Habits with ています

changes.before: Te imasu can express a repeated habit; te imashita describes a former habit.
changes.after: ています can express a repeated habit; ていました describes a former habit.

changes.before: Plain form plus shi lists related points supporting the same view. A conclusion may follow or remain understood.
changes.after: Plain form plus し lists related points supporting the same view. A conclusion may follow or remain understood.

changes.before: Nouns and na-adjectives take dashi; soreni adds a further point.
changes.after: Nouns and な-adjectives take だし; それに adds a further point.

changes.before: Sorede links a stated reason with its natural result.
changes.after: それで links a stated reason with its natural result.

changes.before: Particles after toki
changes.after: Particles after とき

changes.before: Toki is a noun and can take particles such as wa, ni or ya as required.
changes.after: とき is a noun and can take particles such as は, に or や as required.

changes.before: Place the particle after the whole toki phrase.
changes.after: Place the particle after the whole とき phrase.

changes.before: Verb stem without masu
changes.after: Verb stem without ます

changes.before: Verb in te/de form
changes.after: Verb in て/で form

changes.before: Verb in ta/da form
changes.after: Verb in た/だ form

changes.before: An intransitive te-form plus imasu describes a state remaining after a change. Use ga when describing what is observed.
changes.after: An intransitive て-form plus います describes a state remaining after a change. Use が when describing what is observed.

changes.before: Unlike an ongoing action, kowarete imasu normally means already broken.
changes.after: Unlike an ongoing action, 壊れています normally means already broken.

changes.before: Te shimaimasu emphasizes full completion; te shimaimashita can also express regret about an unwanted event.
changes.after: てしまいます emphasizes full completion; てしまいました can also express regret about an unwanted event.

changes.before: Ni for a destination
changes.after: に for a destination

changes.before: Ikimasu, kimasu and kaerimasu take ni for a destination; e can also mark direction.
changes.after: 行きます, 来ます and 帰ります take に for a destination; へ can also mark direction.

changes.before: Distinguish destination ni from action-location de.
changes.after: Distinguish destination に from action-location で.

changes.before: Sore refers to a matter, sono modifies a noun, and sou refers to a way or content just mentioned.
changes.after: それ refers to a matter, その modifies a noun, and そう refers to a way or content just mentioned.

changes.before: Arimashita on finding something
changes.after: ありました on finding something

changes.before: Arimashita can announce the discovery of something being sought, rather than merely past existence.
changes.after: ありました can announce the discovery of something being sought, rather than merely past existence.

changes.before: Keeping de and ni after dokoka
changes.after: Keeping で and に after どこか

changes.before: Dokoka de indicates an unspecified action location; dokoka ni an unspecified place of existence or destination.
changes.after: どこか で indicates an unspecified action location; どこか に an unspecified place of existence or destination.

changes.before: De and ni must remain, unlike some uses of e or wo.
changes.after: で and に must remain, unlike some uses of へ or を.

changes.before: Verb in te/de form
changes.after: Verb in て/で form

changes.before: Verb in te/de form
changes.after: Verb in て/で form

changes.before: Verb in te/de form
changes.after: Verb in て/で form

changes.before: A transitive verb with te arimasu describes the remaining result of someone's deliberate action. The object takes ga or topical wa.
changes.after: A transitive verb with てあります describes the remaining result of someone's deliberate action. The object takes が or topical は.

changes.before: Te imasu describes a state; te arimasu suggests intentional arrangement.
changes.after: ています describes a state; てあります suggests intentional arrangement.

changes.before: Te okimasu expresses advance preparation, putting things right after use, or leaving a state unchanged.
changes.after: ておきます expresses advance preparation, putting things right after use, or leaving a state unchanged.

changes.before: The conversational contraction is tokimasu.
changes.after: The conversational contraction is ときます.

changes.before: Mada with an affirmative says that an action or state continues.
changes.after: まだ with an affirmative says that an action or state continues.

changes.before: Contrast mada te imasen, meaning not yet done.
changes.after: Contrast まだ ていません, meaning not yet done.

changes.before: Examples with toka
changes.after: Examples with とか

changes.before: Toka introduces a non-exhaustive list of examples, commonly in conversation.
changes.after: とか introduces a non-exhaustive list of examples, commonly in conversation.

changes.before: Toka may also follow the last listed example.
changes.after: とか may also follow the last listed example.

changes.before: Mo after particles
changes.after: も after particles

changes.before: Mo replaces ga and wo but follows retained particles such as ni, de, kara, made and to.
changes.after: も replaces が and を but follows retained particles such as に, で, から, まで and と.

changes.before: E may remain or be omitted before mo.
changes.after: へ may remain or be omitted before も.

changes.before: Verb in te/de form
changes.after: Verb in て/で form

changes.before: Verb in te/de form
changes.after: Verb in て/で form

changes.before: Verb in te/de form
changes.after: Verb in て/で form

changes.before: Group I changes final u-row to o-row plus u; Group II replaces ru with you. Suru becomes shiyou and kuru becomes koyou.
changes.after: Group I changes final う-row to お-row plus う; Group II replaces る with よう. する becomes しよう and 来る becomes 来よう.

changes.before: The volitional corresponds to polite mashou in familiar speech.
changes.after: The volitional corresponds to polite ましょう in familiar speech.

changes.before: The volitional makes a familiar suggestion; to omotte imasu expresses an intention already held.
changes.after: The volitional makes a familiar suggestion; と思っています expresses an intention already held.

changes.before: To omotte imasu can report another person's intention; to omoimasu usually states the speaker's current intention.
changes.after: と思っています can report another person's intention; と思います usually states the speaker's current intention.

changes.before: Intention with tsumori
changes.after: Intention with つもり

changes.before: Dictionary form plus tsumori desu states an intention; nai plus tsumori desu states an intention not to act.
changes.after: Dictionary form plus つもりです states an intention; ない plus つもりです states an intention not to act.

changes.before: Tsumori commonly emphasizes a settled intention.
changes.after: つもり commonly emphasizes a settled intention.

changes.before: A dictionary-form verb or noun plus no precedes yotei desu for a scheduled plan.
changes.after: A dictionary-form verb or noun plus の precedes 予定です for a scheduled plan.

changes.before: Yotei suits arrangements rather than a mere wish.
changes.after: 予定 suits arrangements rather than a mere wish.

changes.before: Mada te imasen says something has not happened or been completed by the present point.
changes.after: まだ ていません says something has not happened or been completed by the present point.

changes.before: Answer a mou question with iie, mada if it is not done yet.
changes.after: Answer a もう question with いいえ, まだ if it is not done yet.

changes.before: Some masu stems function as nouns, such as kaeri for the return journey and yasumi for a break.
changes.after: Some ます stems function as nouns, such as 帰り for the return journey and 休み for a break.

changes.before: Verb in nai form
changes.after: Verb in ない form

changes.before: Verb in te/de form
changes.after: Verb in て/で form

changes.before: An attested stem-noun such as kaeri
changes.after: An attested stem-noun such as 帰り

changes.before: Ta hou ga ii desu recommends an action; nai hou ga ii desu advises against it.
changes.after: たほうがいいです recommends an action; ないほうがいいです advises against it.

changes.before: This is directed advice and can be stronger than a tara ii suggestion.
changes.after: This is directed advice and can be stronger than a たらいい suggestion.

changes.before: Prediction with deshou
changes.after: Prediction with でしょう

changes.before: Plain form plus deshou expresses a prediction; omit da after nouns and na-adjectives.
changes.after: Plain form plus でしょう expresses a prediction; omit だ after nouns and な-adjectives.

changes.before: Possibility with kamoshiremasen
changes.after: Possibility with かもしれません

changes.before: Plain form plus kamoshiremasen presents an uncertain possibility; omit noun and na-adjective da.
changes.after: Plain form plus かもしれません presents an uncertain possibility; omit noun and な-adjective だ.

changes.before: It usually expresses less certainty than deshou.
changes.after: It usually expresses less certainty than でしょう.

changes.before: Mashou can offer an action that the speaker will undertake.
changes.after: ましょう can offer an action that the speaker will undertake.

changes.before: A quantity plus de marks a time allowance or budget within which something is possible.
changes.after: A quantity plus で marks a time allowance or budget within which something is possible.

changes.before: Distinguish completion within a time limit from a duration without de.
changes.after: Distinguish completion within a time limit from a duration without で.

changes.before: Use nanika plus adjective plus mono or koto, and dokoka plus adjective plus tokoro for an unspecified item or place.
changes.after: Use 何か plus adjective plus 物 or 事, and どこか plus adjective plus 所 for an unspecified item or place.

changes.before: Retain the final noun: nanika tsumetai mono, rather than placing the adjective before nanika.
changes.after: Retain the final noun: 何か冷たい物, rather than placing the adjective before 何か.

changes.before: Verb in nai form
changes.after: Verb in ない form

changes.before: Predicted clause, omitting final noun/na-adjective da
changes.after: Predicted clause, omitting final noun/な-adjective だ

changes.before: Possible plain clause, omitting noun/na-adjective da
changes.after: Possible plain clause, omitting noun/な-adjective だ

changes.before: Verb stem without masu
changes.after: Verb stem without ます

changes.before: Adjective modifying mono
changes.after: Adjective modifying 物

changes.before: Group I commands change the ending to the e-row; Group II replaces ru with ro; suru becomes shiro and kuru becomes koi. A prohibition uses dictionary form plus na.
changes.after: Group I commands change the ending to the え-row; Group II replaces る with ろ; する becomes しろ and 来る becomes 来い. A prohibition uses dictionary form plus な.

changes.before: Kureru has kurero; avoid mechanically applying it to state verbs such as aru.
changes.after: くれる has くれろ; avoid mechanically applying it to state verbs such as ある.

changes.before: Nasai can be used by responsible adults such as parents or teachers, but not toward superiors.
changes.after: なさい can be used by responsible adults such as parents or teachers, but not toward superiors.

changes.before: To before kaite arimasu or yomimasu marks written content or its reading.
changes.after: と before 書いてあります or 読みます marks written content or its reading.

changes.before: Quoted text may appear in quotation marks; to here does not mean together with.
changes.after: Quoted text may appear in quotation marks; と here does not mean together with.

changes.before: X wa Y to iu imi desu explains X; ask dou iu imi desu ka for its meaning.
changes.after: X は Y という意味です explains X; ask どういう意味ですか for its meaning.

changes.before: Plain form plus to itte imashita relays what another person said.
changes.after: Plain form plus と言っていました relays what another person said.

changes.before: A plain message plus to tsutaete itadakemasen ka politely asks someone to relay it.
changes.after: A plain message plus と伝えていただけませんか politely asks someone to relay it.

changes.before: A sentence ending in a noun needs da before to.
changes.after: A sentence ending in a noun needs だ before to.

changes.before: Verb stem without masu
changes.after: Verb stem without ます

changes.before: Message, retaining noun-final da
changes.after: Message, retaining noun-final だ

changes.before: Dictionary or ta-form plus toori ni, or noun plus no toori ni, means following the indicated model.
changes.after: Dictionary or た-form plus とおりに, or noun plus のとおりに, means following the indicated model.

changes.before: Ta can refer to an observed model; dictionary form can refer to instructions being given.
changes.after: た can refer to an observed model; dictionary form can refer to instructions being given.

changes.before: Ta-form plus ato de or noun plus no ato de places an action after another completed event.
changes.after: た-form plus あとで or noun plus のあとで places an action after another completed event.

changes.before: It stresses sequence without necessarily making the first action a preparation as te kara can.
changes.after: It stresses sequence without necessarily making the first action a preparation as てから can.

changes.before: Te or naide gives a state accompanying the main action. Naide can also mean choosing another action instead.
changes.after: て or ないで gives a state accompanying the main action. ないで can also mean choosing another action instead.

changes.before: The actions normally share a subject; do not replace intentional naide here with nakute.
changes.after: The actions normally share a subject; do not replace intentional ないで here with なくて.

changes.before: Verb in ta/da form
changes.after: Verb in た/だ form

changes.before: Verb in te/de form
changes.after: Verb in て/で form

changes.before: Group I changes final sound to e-row plus ba; Group II replaces ru with reba; suru becomes sureba and kuru becomes kureba. Nai becomes nakereba; i-adjectives use kereba.
changes.after: Group I changes final sound to え-row plus ば; Group II replaces る with れば; する becomes すれば and 来る becomes 来れば. ない becomes なければ; い-adjectives use ければ.

changes.before: Nouns and na-adjectives use nara.
changes.after: Nouns and な-adjectives use なら.

changes.before: Using ba and distinguishing conditionals
changes.after: Using ば and distinguishing conditionals

changes.before: Ba states a condition for a result. To often gives an automatic consequence; tara can give what happens after a condition is fulfilled.
changes.after: ば states a condition for a result. と often gives an automatic consequence; たら can give what happens after a condition is fulfilled.

changes.before: With the same subject and an intentional first action, commands or volition do not freely follow ba.
changes.after: With the same subject and an intentional first action, commands or volition do not freely follow ば.

changes.before: A question word plus conditional plus ii desu ka asks for the appropriate action.
changes.after: A question word plus conditional plus いいですか asks for the appropriate action.

changes.before: It is close in function to tara ii desu ka, rather than a simple correctness question.
changes.after: It is close in function to たらいいですか, rather than a simple correctness question.

changes.before: Nara as a topic response
changes.after: なら as a topic response

changes.before: Noun plus nara offers advice or information about a topic just raised.
changes.after: Noun plus なら offers advice or information about a topic just raised.

changes.before: Wa arimasen ka asks whether the listener knows of a suitable item.
changes.after: は ありません か asks whether the listener knows of a suitable item.

changes.before: I-adjective in kereba form
changes.after: い-adjective in ければ form

changes.before: Verb in ba-conditional form
changes.after: Verb in ば-conditional form

changes.before: Verb in ba-conditional form
changes.after: Verb in ば-conditional form

changes.before: A goal with you ni
changes.after: A goal with ように

changes.before: Dictionary or nai-form plus you ni gives a desired state, often ability or something not directly controlled by will.
changes.after: Dictionary or ない-form plus ように gives a desired state, often ability or something not directly controlled by will.

changes.before: Contrast tame ni, commonly used for an intentional action as a purpose.
changes.after: Contrast ために, commonly used for an intentional action as a purpose.

changes.before: An ability verb plus you ni narimasu describes a new ability. Naku narimasu describes loss of ability or ending a habit.
changes.after: An ability verb plus ようになります describes a new ability. なくなります describes loss of ability or ending a habit.

changes.before: If the change has not occurred, answer mada with a negative.
changes.after: If the change has not occurred, answer まだ with a negative.

changes.before: You ni shite imasu expresses an effort to keep a habit; you ni shite kudasai asks someone to make that effort.
changes.after: ようにしています expresses an effort to keep a habit; ようにしてください asks someone to make that effort.

changes.before: I-adjectives change i to ku; na-adjectives take ni to modify a verb.
changes.after: い-adjectives change い to く; な-adjectives take に to modify a verb.

changes.before: Ii becomes yoku.
changes.after: いい becomes よく.

changes.before: Verb in nai form
changes.after: Verb in ない form

changes.before: Adjective in adverbial ku or ni form
changes.after: Adjective in adverbial く or に form

changes.before: Group I changes final sound to the a-row plus reru; Group II replaces ru with rareru; suru becomes sareru and kuru becomes korareru.
changes.after: Group I changes final sound to the あ-row plus れる; Group II replaces る with られる; する becomes される and 来る becomes 来られる.

changes.before: The affected person is the wa-topic; the actor takes ni before the passive verb.
changes.after: The affected person is the は-topic; the actor takes に before the passive verb.

changes.before: Do not replace every beneficial action with the passive; te morau expresses receiving a favor.
changes.after: Do not replace every beneficial action with the passive; てもらう expresses receiving a favor.

changes.before: Affected person wa, actor ni, possession wo and a passive describe an action affecting a person's possession.
changes.after: Affected person は, actor に, possession を and a passive describe an action affecting a person's possession.

changes.before: Kara commonly marks transformed raw ingredients; de often marks material recognizable in the finished object.
changes.after: から commonly marks transformed raw ingredients; で often marks material recognizable in the finished object.

changes.before: Appositional no
changes.after: Appositional の

changes.before: The first noun with no may identify the role or type of the second noun.
changes.after: The first noun with の may identify the role or type of the second noun.

changes.before: No does not always mean ownership.
changes.after: の does not always mean ownership.

changes.before: Kono, sono and ano before position words such as naka or chikaku locate something relative to an identified object.
changes.after: この, その and あの before position words such as 中 or 近く locate something relative to an identified object.

changes.before: Kono naka can mean inside this object without repeating its name.
changes.after: この 中 can mean inside this object without repeating its name.

changes.before: Relative position word such as naka
changes.after: Relative position word such as 中

changes.before: Nominalizing with no
changes.after: Nominalizing with の

changes.before: Add no after a plain-form verb to use an event as a noun phrase.
changes.after: Add の after a plain-form verb to use an event as a noun phrase.

changes.before: The particle after no marks the role of the entire clause.
changes.after: The particle after の marks the role of the entire clause.

changes.before: Dictionary form plus no wa plus an adjective makes an activity the topic of an evaluation.
changes.after: Dictionary form plus のは plus an adjective makes an activity the topic of an evaluation.

changes.before: Distinguish topical no wa from no ga marking an object of preference or ability.
changes.after: Distinguish topical のは from のが marking an object of preference or ability.

changes.before: Preferences and ability with no ga
changes.after: Preferences and ability with のが

changes.before: Dictionary form plus no ga precedes adjectives such as suki, jouzu and hayai to identify the activity concerned.
changes.after: Dictionary form plus のが precedes adjectives such as 好き, 上手 and 速い to identify the activity concerned.

changes.before: The person with that preference or ability can be a separate wa-topic.
changes.after: The person with that preference or ability can be a separate は-topic.

changes.before: Dictionary form plus no wo wasuremashita says one forgot to perform an action.
changes.after: Dictionary form plus のを忘れました says one forgot to perform an action.

changes.before: Plain form plus no wo shitte imasu ka asks whether someone knows an event-related fact.
changes.after: Plain form plus のを知っていますか asks whether someone knows an event-related fact.

changes.before: For news learned through the question, reply shirimasen deshita; for an unknown address, shirimasen remains appropriate.
changes.after: For news learned through the question, reply 知りませんでした; for an unknown address, 知りません remains appropriate.

changes.before: Focusing with no wa
changes.after: Focusing with のは

changes.before: Clause plus no wa plus noun desu highlights an identified person, place or time. Nouns and na-adjectives take na before no.
changes.after: Clause plus のは plus noun です highlights an identified person, place or time. Nouns and な-adjectives take な before の.

changes.before: The subject inside the clause normally takes ga rather than wa.
changes.after: The subject inside the clause normally takes が rather than は.

changes.before: Background clause with a ga-marked subject
changes.after: Background clause with a が-marked subject

changes.before: Causes with te and de
changes.after: Causes with て and で

changes.before: Te, nakute, kute and de can link a cause to an emotion or unintended result; noun de marks causes such as accidents.
changes.after: て, なくて, くて and で can link a cause to an emotion or unintended result; noun で marks causes such as accidents.

changes.before: Do not freely place an invitation, intention or command after this causal construction; use kara when appropriate.
changes.after: Do not freely place an invitation, intention or command after this causal construction; use から when appropriate.

changes.before: Giving a reason with node
changes.after: Giving a reason with ので

changes.before: Plain form plus node gives a relatively matter-of-fact reason; nouns and na-adjectives take na node.
changes.after: Plain form plus ので gives a relatively matter-of-fact reason; nouns and な-adjectives take なので.

changes.before: Dictionary form plus tochuu de, or noun plus no tochuu de, marks a point during an activity or journey.
changes.after: Dictionary form plus 途中で, or noun plus の途中で, marks a point during an activity or journey.

changes.before: De identifies where or when something intervenes rather than the destination.
changes.after: で identifies where or when something intervenes rather than the destination.

changes.before: Cause in verb te/de form
changes.after: Cause in verb て/で form

changes.before: Plain-form reason with na after nouns/na-adjectives
changes.after: Plain-form reason with な after nouns/な-adjectives

changes.before: Put a question in plain form and add ka to embed it in a larger sentence. Omit da after nouns and na-adjectives.
changes.after: Put a question in plain form and add か to embed it in a larger sentence. Omit だ after nouns and な-adjectives.

changes.before: Keep the question word; do not insert desu ka inside the sentence.
changes.after: Keep the question word; do not insert ですか inside the sentence.

changes.before: Plain form plus ka dou ka embeds a yes-or-no question.
changes.after: Plain form plus かどうか embeds a yes-or-no question.

changes.before: Do not combine a question word such as itsu with ka dou ka; use itsu ... ka.
changes.after: Do not combine a question word such as いつ with かどうか; use いつ ... か.

changes.before: Te mimasu means trying an action to experience it or see the result.
changes.after: てみます means trying an action to experience it or see the result.

changes.before: Miru here does not literally mean looking.
changes.after: 見る here does not literally mean looking.

changes.before: Degree nouns with sa
changes.after: Degree nouns with さ

changes.before: Replace final i of an i-adjective with sa to form a degree noun such as nagasa or omosa.
changes.after: Replace final い of an い-adjective with さ to form a degree noun such as 長さ or 重さ.

changes.before: Softening a question with deshou ka
changes.after: Softening a question with でしょうか

changes.before: Deshou ka makes a question less direct, often when seeking an opinion or uncertain information.
changes.after: でしょうか makes a question less direct, often when seeking an opinion or uncertain information.

changes.before: Plain embedded question with a question word, without final da
changes.after: Plain embedded question with a question word, without final だ

changes.before: Plain yes/no question without final da
changes.after: Plain yes/の question without final だ

changes.before: Verb in te/de form
